summary: Retire the persisted `@chatgpt` handle (owner ruling 2026-07-21 M2: the OpenAI assistant is @openai, never @chatgpt; M5: the local CLI is no longer a distinct @-mention assistant). Epic #1873 W6 — the ONE-WAY removal of the legacy `chatgpt` flat handle/alias from the registry tables, shipped WITH the delete of the bridge route/gate/fixtures in the same PR. `@chatgpt` was a dev-only local-CLI bridge (a hardcoded route + Codex-CLI producer), NOT a boot-seeded principal — the boot seeds mint only cinatra/wordpress/drupal handles (src/lib/auth.ts) and the only seeded alias is the immutable `cinatra` builtin, so a code-seeded database has NEITHER a chatgpt handle nor a chatgpt alias (this migration is a NO-OP there, ledger-faked on a fresh install). It exists to converge any operator DB where a `chatgpt` row was persisted at runtime (e.g. a manual namespace-primitive UPDATE) to the post-ruling state. Two existence-guarded (to_regclass) one-way DELETEs — assistant_handles WHERE handle='chatgpt' and assistant_tag_alias WHERE alias='chatgpt' — each idempotent (a re-run matches zero rows) and a partial/fresh DB where a registry table is absent RETURNs early. DESTRUCTIVE (data removal): a fail-loud postcondition RAISEs (rolling the single node-pg-migrate transaction back, no partial apply) if any chatgpt handle/alias row survives. No version bump / Graphiti re-projection (a retired flat handle is never projected). down() is IRREVERSIBLE (throws): the flat `chatgpt` token is retired, not renamed — there is no `@chatgpt` handle to restore the deleted rows to, so a faithful reverse mapping does not exist; same class as core__0064; restore from a backup to roll back. SEQ 0083 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0082_dashboard-twin-scope-tuple-backfill, #1898); a concurrent lane landing an intervening seq first makes a rename-only renumber normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train; the runner tolerates sequence gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
